title: Diesel gave way, gasoline did not
paragraphs: This cycle started with an expiry day. On Wednesday 30 September Brent's November contract stopped trading at $106.31 and December, about $7.50 lower, became the front month. NY Harbor diesel and RBOB gasoline rolled from October to November the same day. Every number in this table is on the new contracts, so the drop from EIA's last physical Brent ($113.96 on Tuesday) to the futures is mostly the roll and the normal premium of prompt oil in a backwardated market, not a crash.

By Friday's close one spread stood apart. Since the last EIA print, the diesel crack fell from $96.00 to $86.80 and the 3-2-1 from $67.04 to $64.65, with Brent lower. The gasoline crack went the other way: from $43.66 to $48.01, up $1.49 on the futures since Wednesday alone. Diesel futures slipped from $4.69 to $4.50 a gallon while Brent December rose from $98.03 to $102.25.

Conclusion for Friday: gasoline crack up, everything else down. That is against the season. September is when refiners switch to cheaper winter-grade gasoline and the gasoline crack normally fades. A gasoline crack that rises in early October points to tight gasoline supply rather than the calendar, while the diesel squeeze is easing. One week is not a trend; watch whether the EIA release on Wednesday 7 October confirms it in the physical prices. Next roll: WTI November expires on Tuesday 20 October.
